newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says Senate tax bill seems better than House.
newsitem.headline: Rubin says Senate tax bill seems better than House.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said the Senate tax cut proposal seems to resolve some of the problems that were in the House version but he stopped short of endorsing the Senate bill.
He said it was "too early in the process" to know whether Congress would pass a tax bill that President Clinton could sign or whether the White House would consider a veto.

Rubin said the Senate version being drawn up by committee chairman William Roth, a Delaware Republican, had resolved several of what the administration sees as problems in the House Ways and Means committee's bill.

"Roth's proposal is an improvement ... in a number of respects," Rubin said, adding that Roth's bill drops the indexing of capital gains for inflation and has a more satisfactory provison on the corporate alternative minimum tax.

But he said the Roth version still falls short of the $35 billion in education-related tax cuts Clinton insisted on in the balanced budget plan, and there are still problems in the way the Senate bill sets up the $500 child tax credit and some of the Hope scholarship provisions for higher education.
He said the lower income families will not be able to get the full tax benefits the way the Republicans have structured the bill.

He said the administration was interested in Roth's proposal for a new kind of Individual Retirement Account for education. "We think it's a concept that has a lot of merit to it. There are some particular details that we think should be worked out somewhat differently," he said.
